info.name: GoRyde - End-to-End Integration Tests
info.description:
GoRyde end-to-end integration test suite (via API Gateway on {{baseUrl}}).

Run order: 00 Authentication -> 01 Driver Setup -> 02 Ride Creation -> 03 Driver Workflow -> 04 Ride Lifecycle -> 05 Payment -> 06 Negative & Authorization Tests.
Run the whole collection top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner or Newman; folders and requests are ordered as dependencies require.

VARIABLES: All state (JWTs, ids, runId) is captured automatically into collection variables by each request's Tests script - no manual copying required. Re-running the collection is safe: the first request generates a fresh runId used to namespace test emails, avoiding duplicate-email 409s.

KNOWN APPLICATION-LEVEL ISSUE (found via source inspection, not introduced by this test suite):
ride-service's RideService.start()/complete() authorize the calling driver by comparing the JWT's
auth-service user id (header X-Authenticated-User-Id, set by the gateway from /internal/auth/validate)
directly against ride.getDriverId(). However ride.driverId is populated by DriverMatchingService from
driver-service's /api/drivers/nearest response, i.e. it is the driver-service Driver table's primary key -
a completely independent id sequence from auth-service's User table. Unless these two ids happen to
coincide numerically for a given test run, POST /api/rides/{id}/start and /complete will return 403
Forbidden for the legitimate assigned driver. This does not affect the driver-service-routed actions
(accept/arriving/arrived), which correctly compare driver-service ids on both sides. The '04 - Ride
Lifecycle' folder's Start Ride / Complete Ride requests print the two ids to the console and flag this
explicitly rather than silently forcing a pass. This is reported per the task instructions rather than
patched, since editing application source code is out of scope for this test suite.
